..
Issued at 231 PM CDT Sun Sep 6 2026

Current Conditions:

Surface high pressure is moving off to the east with southerly flow 
returning across the region. Aloft we still have a ridge in place. 
Embedded in the flow aloft there are several impulses rounding the 
ridge axis over the Red River Valley and spilling over into the 
Northland. Presently this is manifesting as some light echoes on the 
radar, however, not seeing any signs via webcams or sensors that 
this activity is making it to the ground. High res guidance is 
widely scattered with its depiction of simulated radar reflectivity 
through the afternoon and beyond. Which is to be expected in the 
weakly forced regime we find ourselves in. Overall, largely expect 
most the region to stay dry with some isolated light rain showers at 
times. 

Tonight/Labor Day.

Overnight, the ridge axis shifts further east towards the Great
Lakes as a shortwave advances out of the Northern Plains. 
Moisture profiles begin to saturate leading to a slight increase
in PoPs for the overnight and early morning hours across 
northern MN. A few thunderstorms will be possible as well, but 
the environment is lacking deep layer shear which will keep 
storms on the tame side. Through the remainder of the holiday 
the Northland will find itself in the warm sector of an 
approaching system in the Northern Rockies. The continued warm 
air advection and isentropic forcing may lead to off and on rain
chances through the day with mostly cloudy skies. Temperatures 
will be in the 70s with a few low 80s possible. Additionally, 
the southerly winds will see our dew points climb into the upper
60s by the afternoon.

Late Labor Day into Tuesday:

Large scale ascent is expected to increase late Labor Day and 
through Tuesday morning. An upper level trough over the Canadian 
Prairies pushes the ridge completely out of the Northland opening the 
door for southwesterly flow to stream back into the region. One of 
the unique aspects of this incoming set up is the high PWATs that 
the system will have access to. The IVT plots would suggest 
contributions from both the the Gulf and Hurricane Marie. 
Climatology puts the incoming PWATs near the max of climatology.
Despite this wealth of moisture, most of the guidance keeps QPF
fairly moderated. EFI is mainly honing in on areas north of the
International Border as being the hotpots for heavy rainfall, 
likely coinciding with the warm frontal boundary. While we may 
not be the recipients of the highest rain totals we should still
see our fair share with current guidance suggesting around an 
1" for most of MN with lower amounts across the Arrowhead and NW
WI. 

Severe chances start to increase late Monday as well with an upper 
level jet nudging in from the southwest. Instability may be limited 
with high PWATs and lack of mid level lapse rates. With these meager 
ingredients in play the SPC has out western counties outlined in a 
marginal risk (threat level 1 out of 5). Primary hazard would likely 
be hail the size of quarters with damaging winds being a secondary 
threat. Storm activity could be persistent into Tuesday as a low 
level jet strengthens across the Midwest. 

Tuesday will see ongoing showers and storms through the morning. The 
upper level low over the Canadian Prairies will strengthen with a 
noticeable dry slot sweeping in behind the cold front set to move 
through the region. Depending on how quickly the front advances
east the region we could have some lingering severe storm
threat into NW WI in the afternoon. 

Wed - Fri:

On Wednesday the upper level low spins into the Hudson Bay with 
persistent cyclonic flow aloft over the region. Low level moisture 
still looks favorable with mid and upper level moisture questionable 
at the moment. The pattern looks pretty similar to the ones we get 
with isolated showers and more widespread drizzle. Overall, 
expecting a cloudy day with much cooler temperatures. Highs may not 
climb out of the 70s in northern MN with NW WI in the mid and low 
70s. Thursday looks to be the quietest weather day in the upcoming 
week with surface high pressure gliding across the Midwest. Rain 
chances look to return Friday as another front cross through the 
Northland.
